production.name: LOW TIDE
production.logline: A harbour worker follows a rope into the low-tide sand and finds the boat the old harbourmaster swore would come back on its own.
production.synopsis: At dawn Ada walks the harbour wall to check a rope that has hung from an iron ring for twenty years. Jonah, the harbourmaster, tells her ropes only last. At low tide the rope leads her to a half-buried boat, and she brings its nameplate back to him.

script.title: LOW TIDE
script.fountain:
Title: LOW TIDE
Credit: Written by
Author: Pure Alacrity example

[[HOW TO READ THIS
A four-scene example that shows every element the importer reads. It is not a real production.]]

EXT. HARBOUR WALL - DAWN

Grey water, a long stone wall. ADA (30s, oilskin jacket) walks the top of it with a torch she no longer needs.

She stops at an iron ring set into the stone. A rope runs from it down into the water.

ADA
(to herself)
Still here.

[[Practical dawn only. Shoot the wide first while the sky holds.]]

INT. HARBOURMASTER'S OFFICE - DAWN

A kettle on a gas ring. Charts pinned over charts. JONAH (60s) does not look up from the tide table.

JONAH
You went out on the wall again.

ADA
The rope's still there.

JONAH
Ropes last. That's all they do.

He turns the tide table round so she can read it.

EXT. HARBOUR WALL - DAY

Low tide. The rope runs down into wet sand and ends at a small wooden boat, half buried, painted blue once.

Ada climbs down the iron ladder.

ADA (V.O.)
He said it would come back on its own.

CUT TO:

INT. HARBOURMASTER'S OFFICE - DAY

Ada sets a brass nameplate on the desk: BLUE HOUR.

Jonah looks at it for a long time.

JONAH
Put the kettle on.

> THE END <

devNotes.title: The rope is the film
devNotes.body: Every scene should know where the rope is. It is the only thing that connects the wall, the office and the boat.
